written: 2026-11-01, before any pipeline run on this set
labeller: The assistant, not a licensed examiner. Two auditors with different methods worked independently and blind to any pipeline output, then one adjudicator opened the sheets and ruled on each item.

A.method: sheet by sheet in page order
A.limits:
Positions are fractions in the reading frame: the page rotation is removed, so the sheet is 1224 x 792 pt landscape with the title block at the right. PyMuPDF's default frame keeps /Rotate 270 and is 792 x 1224. To convert, fx_default = y and fy_default = 1 - x.

This PDF is a 6-sheet extract, so the sheets named in D05 to D11 may exist in the full set. Each is reported because it is missing from this file.

The set has no cover sheet, sheet index or code summary, so kind 1 had nothing to compare and kind 3 covers only the area lines. Sheet numbers are unique, and there are no door tags or door schedule, so the door half of kind 5 could not be done. Door locations were compared between plans and elevations only. There are also no sections, details or roof plan, so roof and stair heights were checked only through elevation level marks and plan tread counts.

No corridor or stair width is printed. Kind 11 could only confirm which doors exist, and no exit count or width is printed to check.

Lengths were measured from vector line work at half the stated scale, to about 0.05 ft. The D22 areas are estimates, partly from the key plan. Recess and platform sizes are measured, not printed.

Schedule cells came from the text layer and were spot-checked on the picture, not read cell by cell in images. The schedule tiles not viewed one by one were covered by that parse. Other tiles left unviewed held only material already seen at 100 dpi, such as title blocks or blank sheet. The review advisor was rate-limited, so this list has no second review. Only the PDF and files in my scratch folder were opened.

B.limits: Position fractions use the sheet turned upright: landscape, 1224 x 792 pt, title block at right, x from left, y from top. Each PDF page carries /Rotate 270, so a default render is portrait; to convert, portrait x fraction = y and portrait y fraction = 1 - x. The file is 6 sheets of a larger set (it refers to at least 8 sheets it does not hold). Sheet numbers are unique. There is no sheet index, code summary, door schedule, window schedule, section, roof plan or reflected ceiling plan, so kinds 1 and 3 had little to compare, door tag checks had nothing to run on, and roof and floor-to-floor checks rest on elevations only. Stair and corridor widths are not printed; measured flight widths are about 4'-3 for the exit stairs and 5'-2 for Stair 1, corridor about 6'-6. The sheets are half size: drawn scale measures 2.25 pt/ft on plans and 3.375 pt/ft on elevations, which equals the stated scale on a 22 x 34 sheet, not on this 11 x 17 page. Measured lengths on plans are good to about 3 in. Area measurements against the printed notes are approximate. The set comes from a coordinated model: grid positions, levels and most geometry agree on every sheet, so most findings are tags, numbering, title block and drafting items. Several items are marked unsure because the answer may sit on a sheet outside this excerpt.

adjudicator_notes: RESULT. 45 items from 36 Auditor A entries and 39 Auditor B entries: 20 real, 15 likely, 10 not_a_defect. Every auditor entry maps to at least one item. No new item was added: wing end doors, level heights, stair positions, room positions across floors and 102 schedule rows were all checked and gave nothing beyond the auditors' lists. SHEET-LEVEL FINDINGS. No sheet index exists on any of the 6 sheets, so kind 1 has only the check that the 6 sheet numbers are unique and that view tags name their own sheet, which they do. The file looks like a six-sheet excerpt, so J11 to J17 are real for the set as supplied and might clear in a full set. There is no code or project summary, only the two area notes (kind 3). No door tags and no corridor or stair width dimensions exist (kinds 5, 11). CORRECTIONS TO THE AUDITORS. Auditor A counted 10 A-301 strings; the sheets have 12, as Auditor B said. Auditor A's 49 first floor window openings is confirmed from elevation counts. Printed-against-drawn was measured on all 73 dimension values on 4 sheets by tick marks: all agree within about 1 inch at half the stated scale, so there is no kind 8 value failure. COVERAGE. A-101 (page 0), first floor composition plan, key plan, area note: 60 room tags against 59 rows both ways; 16 callout markers; 27 dimension values; 32 column and 20 row bubbles; 3 stairs plus the steel stair against A-102; 55 key plan segments; area note arithmetic; 0 window tags. A-102 (page 1), second floor composition plan, key plan, area note: 43 room tags against 43 rows both ways; 50 window tags against wall openings and elevations; 15 callout markers; 32 column and 20 row bubbles; no dimension strings exist on this sheet; both total area sums; recess and platform extents measured. A-201 (page 2), South Elevations, 2 views: 12 dimension values; 27 distinct column bubbles against 32; 12 level tags, drawn heights checked on view 1; 30 windows per floor; 5 callouts. A-202 (page 3), East and West Elevations: 13 dimension values; 20 bubbles on each view; 13 level tags, drawn heights checked on the East view; doors compared with A-101, namely wing end doors, stair exit doors and double doors; 2 callouts. A-203 (page 4), North Elevations, 2 views: 21 dimension values; all 32 column bubbles; 14 level tags; 19 windows per floor; doors on the north face compared with A-101, and the second floor double door compared with A-102; 3 callouts. I-601 (page 5), finish schedules and notes: 102 rows (59 + 43), checked by room type for consistent finishes, which found only rows 201 and 255; 13 notes; title block compared across all 6 sheets. COULD NOT READ. The FIRST FLOOR value on the A-202 East Elevation is covered by TOF and was read from the text layer only. Part of the A-203 view 2 first floor windows is hidden behind a screen wall; the visible tops were counted. The floor 2 area method is not stated on any sheet, so J32 stays likely.

items.statement: Plan labels, tags and grid bubbles collide in 8 places on three sheets: 4 on A-101, 2 on A-102, 2 on A-202. On A-102 one of the two places is the six north wall window tags lying under the heavy dashed line.
items.evidence: A-101: 'D.I. TOILET' runs into 'ELEC.'; 'COMM.' runs into 'D.I. TOILET'; the A-406 marker covers 'RECEPTION/CQ' and '106'; 'VEST.' touches '1ST SGT.'. A-102: the 2/A-302 marker touches 'CLASSROOM'. A-202: bubbles 'K' and 'K.2' overlap and read 'KK.2' and 'K.2K'.
items.reason: Every collision is visible, but each string can still be read, so these are cosmetic.

items.statement: EAVE is misspelled on all six level tags.
items.evidence: 'EVE HEIGHT' '32'-0"'.
items.reason: All six tags read EVE in the text layer and the picture.

items.where: Level marks, for example A-201 at (0.788, 0.177) and (0.796, 0.209).
items.statement: The level named ROOF is 4'-0" below the eave on all three elevation sheets, and the metal panel wall continues above it, so the name does not describe what it marks.
items.evidence: 'EVE HEIGHT' '32'-0"' against 'ROOF' '28'-0"'. Measured on A-201 and A-202, both levels sit at their printed heights above FIRST FLOOR.
items.reason: The heights are drawn as printed and agree on all three sheets, and no sheet gives a conflicting roof height, so this is a naming habit.
